results.name: Inside Help TDS: Hotejka, Cloudflare Pages and Predictive Detection
results.description: Since April 2017, a Russian-language affiliate program called Hotejka, believed to be a rebrand of ROI777, has operated the Help Traffic Distribution System (TDS), delivering tech support scams to victims. The operation uses browser fingerprinting and geolocation to redirect users through compromised websites, malvertising, social media, and spam to fake Microsoft security alerts that lock browsers and display fraudulent phone numbers. When victims call, operators from call centers guide them to install remote desktop tools like UltraViewer, granting complete system access for ongoing exploitation. Since April 2026, Hotejka has created over 20,000 disposable domains on free Cloudflare Pages infrastructure, generating approximately 300 new domains daily. Affiliates including Balada Injector, Detour Dog, and DollyWay drive traffic to the TDS. Infoblox developed predictive detection algorithms that identify malicious domains approximately seven days before deployment, reducing customer exposure from 4% to 0.5...

results.name: BREAK THE SILENCE: Tracking Silent Lynx Through Exposed Infrastructure
results.description: Silent Lynx, a persistent cyber espionage threat actor, has conducted targeted intrusion campaigns against government ministries, diplomatic missions, and civil society organizations across Central Asia since 2024. The group focuses on high-value public sector organizations in Commonwealth of Independent States countries, leveraging spear-phishing campaigns through compromised government email accounts and malware staging via GitHub. Operations from late 2024 through 2026 reveal extensive infrastructure including exposed open directories, newly registered domains, and GitHub repositories. The actor employs lightweight reverse shells, PowerShell scripts, proprietary tools, and commodity utilities. Recent activity shows adoption of exploit-assisted delivery via CVE-2025-8088, expanding focus on Linux systems, and interest in FortiWeb vulnerability CVE-2025-25257. results.name: AI-Powered Espionage Campaign Targets Government Linux Infrastructure
results.description: An espionage campaign tracked as CL-UNK-1211 targeted government entities and state-affiliated infrastructure between October 2025 and April 2026, utilizing AI-generated payloads containing conversational annotations suggesting LLM or automated AI agent involvement. Attackers focused on Linux environments deploying web shells, custom cross-platform backdoors including SysGoRAT malware, and open-source tools to maintain persistent access. Operations included extensive reconnaissance, database dumping, mailbox enumeration targeting social media accounts linked to government emails, and sophisticated defense evasion techniques such as disabling endpoint protections, erasing system logs, and planting deceptive red-team markers to disguise malicious activity as legitimate security assessments.

results.name: KGB RAT: A Fully Undetectable Windows Trojan Built to Spy, Steal, and Terrorize
results.description: KGB RAT is a Windows Remote Access Trojan actively promoted on underground forums since late 2025, marketed deceptively as a legitimate administration tool. Sold through a Malware-as-a-Service model with pricing from $150 to $800, it features credential theft, keylogging, hidden desktop takeover, ransomware capabilities, and psychological harassment functions including screamers and forced blue screens. The tool ships with a built-in FUD crypter updated daily to evade Windows Defender, requires no port forwarding for C2 connectivity, and delivers Telegram-based notifications. Evidence suggests development began in early 2022. Based on NjRAT foundation, it targets multiple operators sharing a common builder, with at least one deployment featuring an active CryptoClipper module for cryptocurrency wallet address swapping.

results.name: Inside a PaperCut Attacker's AI Toolkit: Agent Instructions, Exploit Code, a Second RCE, and Victims Across 45+ Countries
results.description: Three exposed directories on infrastructure at 45.142.193[.]132 revealed an AI-orchestrated campaign targeting PaperCut NG/MF print management software. The exposed workbench contained AI-agent instructions, exploit code, operational logs, and post-exploitation tooling. Attackers exploited CVE-2026-81578 and CVE-2026-82078 through a Tapestry vulnerability chain, and developed a second RCE path via XML-RPC API abuse. The campaign deployed automated exploitation at scale using hundreds of AI agents running through OpenAI Codex and DeepSeek models. Post-exploitation activity included Windows credential harvesting, LSA secret extraction, reverse SOCKS5 pivoting using chisel, Metasploit automation, and Active Directory domain compromise. The actor's files documented 1,005 hosts across 45 countries in their reconnaissance pool, with 46 confirmed Active Directory domain compromises and 45 targets maintaining live internal access pivots at time of discovery.

results.name: DragonForce Ransomware Profile: From Affiliate Program to Cybercrime Cartel
results.description: DragonForce is a financially motivated ransomware operation that emerged in August 2023, initially using leaked LockBit 3.0 code and later transitioning to Conti v3-based variants. Operating as a Ransomware-as-a-Service model, they offer affiliates an 80% revenue share and comprehensive management tools. By March 2025, they evolved into a 'cartel' structure, providing white-label services. Their attacks primarily target organizations in the US and UK, spanning multiple sectors including manufacturing, professional services, retail, healthcare, and technology. The group actively recruits developers and reverse engineers while offering specialized data analysis services to help affiliates maximize extortion pressure. Notable incidents include a major MSP breach in May 2025 exploiting SimpleHelp vulnerabilities, cascading compromise across multiple client networks.
targeted_countries: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

results.name: How AI Agents Turned One Exposed Endpoint into a Server Takeover
results.description: An investigation revealed the first confirmed incident where large language model-driven AI agents executed substantial portions of an attack. Within 24 hours, attackers exploited an exposed job-submission feature on an Apache Tomcat server running Spring Batch, requiring no authentication, zero-days, or new malware. The attacker used Cairn, an open-source AI agent orchestration platform, identified on the attacking infrastructure. Commands were executed through JavaScript via Nashorn engine, with results extracted through error messages in 1,800-byte chunks across hundreds of sequential requests. The attacker recovered plaintext database credentials from configuration files, enabled xp_cmdshell, and escalated privileges using PrintSpoofer and GodPotato tools to achieve SYSTEM access. Registry hives were extracted, administrator accounts created, and artifacts deleted. results.name: PEERSTITCH, a Stealthy FortiGate Implant
results.description: A sophisticated multi-stage network intrusion against a telecommunications organization in September 2024 exploited CVE-2024-47575 on a FortiManager appliance, exfiltrating configurations and cryptographic material for over 500 managed FortiGate firewalls. Attackers then exploited CVE-2025-61624 to deploy PEERSTITCH, a novel memory-resident ARM64 malware that leaves no disk artifacts or network traces. The implant operates by patching running processes, creating covert inter-process communication channels between system daemons, and intercepting network traffic. Additional attack vectors included weaponizing Apache mod_md for reverse shell command and control, impersonating the FortiManager platform to compromise downstream devices, and deploying extensive anti-forensic measures. The intrusion demonstrates advanced tradecraft consistent with nation-state actors, highlighting the critical risk of centralized edge management platforms.

results.name: Beyond the clipboard: The evolving tradecraft of ClickFix
results.description: Threat actors continue to evolve ClickFix tactics, moving beyond simple clipboard-based social engineering to more sophisticated attack chains. Recent campaigns leverage malvertising through typosquatting, SEO poisoning, and compromised websites to deliver fake verification prompts. These attacks now employ elaborate PowerShell scripts with animated progress bars to mimic legitimate security checks. Observed payloads include Node.js-based RATs like DuskDesk, lateral movement techniques targeting domain controllers via WinRM and SSH tunnels, and steganographic delivery chains hiding executables within PNG files. Some campaigns utilize browser-cache-seeded attacks that detect the victim's browser and retrieve staged payloads from cached files. Defense requires user training to recognize social engineering, application control policies, and behavioral monitoring for suspicious command execution patterns and persistence mechanisms.

results.name: Ivanti CVE-2026-104935: Zero-Day Chain Exploited in Operation Innovate
results.description: Ivanti has released emergency security updates after attackers exploited a chain of three zero-day vulnerabilities in Connect Secure VPN appliances to gain root-level access without authentication. The attack began on October 3, targeting an appliance running version 22.8R2.4. Two vulnerabilities are tracked as CVE-2026-104935 with a CVSS score of 8.6, involving an authentication bypass and remote code execution through manipulated CGI requests and malicious file uploads. A third unpatched vulnerability allows privilege escalation to root by manipulating a privileged service through memory modification. While patches address the authentication bypass and RCE, the privilege escalation flaw remains unresolved. CISA added the vulnerability to its KEV catalog with an October 16 remediation deadline for federal agencies.
